summary: Delphine's arcade motorcycle racing series, mixing road racing, motocross, traffic, freestyle, handheld spin-offs, and later Artefacts/Microids revivals.

entries.title: Moto Racer
entries.definitive_edition: Windows primary; PlayStation for extra tracks

emulation.notes: Use Windows for the main route and DuckStation for PlayStation-exclusive tracks.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC Direct3D presentation with modern compatibility; PlayStation extras in emulator

primary.why: Moto Racer was praised as a standout PC arcade racer, with Direct3D visuals and PC LAN/Internet multiplayer. The PlayStation conversion adds two tracks, so Windows is the fidelity primary while PlayStation is a secondary route for those extra tracks.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatible PC or preservation setup; use the PlayStation version in DuckStation only for its two extra tracks.

secondary.exclusive_content: PlayStation conversion adds two tracks for a total of ten instead of the PC version's eight.
secondary.what_to_play: Play or sample the PlayStation-exclusive tracks after the Windows main route.
secondary.why: Windows is the higher-fidelity main route; PlayStation has sourced extra track content.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC release with Direct3D presentation, eight tracks, LAN/Internet multiplayer, and unlockables.
Strong console conversion with split-screen multiplayer and two additional tracks.
all_releases.reason: secondary: play for the two PlayStation-exclusive tracks.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the stronger-fidelity route; PlayStation adds two tracks.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse the original with the 2011 Moto Racer 15th Anniversary remake.

emulation.notes: Use Windows for the main route; use DuckStation only for PlayStation split-screen preservation.

primary.why: Moto Racer 2 released for PlayStation and Windows with 32 race tracks, 16 motorcycles, and a level editor. Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route; PlayStation remains secondary only for local split-screen preservation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatible PC setup; use PlayStation only for split-screen couch multiplayer if desired.

secondary.what_to_play: Use PlayStation only if preserving couch split-screen play.
secondary.why: Windows is the fidelity route; PlayStation's split-screen format is the sourced console-specific mode.

all_releases.reason: secondary: preserve split-screen mode, lower fidelity than PC.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release with configurable fidelity, 32 tracks, 16 motorcycles, and level editor.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the fidelity/editor route; PlayStation is useful only for split-screen local multiplayer.

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution or original PlayStation hardware.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PlayStation presentation with emulator upscaling

primary.why: Moto Racer World Tour is sourced as a PlayStation-only Moto Racer entry with World Tour Championship, arcade, traffic, dragster, and freestyle modes. With no other platform documented, PlayStation is the only complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version in DuckStation at high internal resolution or on original hardware.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced release, with multiple arcade motorcycle race modes.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one sourced platform route; no secondary content route.

emulation.notes: Use a compatible Windows setup or VM.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PC presentation with modern compatibility scaling

primary.why: Moto Racer 3 is sourced as a Windows-only entry with speed, supercross/motocross, freestyle, trial, traffic, unlocks, and online play. With no other platform documented, Windows is the definitive route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatible PC or preservation setup.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced release, with multiple motorcycle-racing disciplines and online play.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one sourced platform route; no secondary content route.

emulation.notes: Use accurate GBA emulation or original hardware; link-cable multiplayer requires compatible hardware/emulation support.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original GBA presentation with modern display scaling

primary.why: Moto Racer Advance is sourced as a Game Boy Advance-only entry with GP, motocross, traffic, progression mode, hidden bikes, and up to four-player link cable support. With no other platform documented, GBA is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Game Boy Advance hardware, Analogue Pocket, mGBA, or another accurate GBA emulator.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced release, built for GBA with pseudo-3D racing and link-cable multiplayer.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one sourced platform route; no secondary content route.

emulation.notes: Use DS hardware or accurate DS emulation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original DS dual-screen presentation with emulator scaling

primary.why: Moto Racer DS is sourced as a Nintendo DS-only series entry with Moto GP, Traffic, Supercross, Freestyle, and multiplayer modes. With no other platform documented, DS is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo DS/3DS hardware or a compatible DS emulator.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced release, with multiple motorcycle-racing modes and DS multiplayer.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one sourced platform route; no secondary content route.

entries.title: Moto Racer 15th Anniversary

emulation.notes: Use a compatible Windows setup if owned; legacy iOS access may be limited.

primary.why: Moto Racer 15th Anniversary is sourced as a 2011 remake released for iOS and Windows. Windows is the higher-fidelity and more preservable route; iOS is a mobile route with no sourced content advantage.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version if already owned on a compatible PC setup; iOS preservation depends on an owned legacy app install.

all_releases.reason: skip: mobile route and no sourced content advantage over Windows.
primary: higher-fidelity and more preservable version of the remake.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a remake/revival, not the original 1997 game.

entries.title: Moto Racer 4

emulation.notes: Run natively on Windows if owned; macOS/console/Switch are alternate access routes.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC release at highest stable settings

primary.why: Moto Racer 4 released for Windows, macOS, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch using Unreal Engine 4. Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route; the console and Switch releases have no sourced exclusive content advantage.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version if owned, with the highest stable resolution/settings; use console versions only as access alternatives.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release using Unreal Engine 4 with configurable fidelity.

all_releases.reason: skip: computer access route but no sourced content advantage over Windows.
skip: console access route and no sourced content advantage over Windows.
skip: console access route and no sourced content advantage over Windows.
skip: portable access route and no sourced content advantage over Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced complete edition beyond the listed releases.
